'''Batch cryptography''' is a field of [[cryptology]] focused on the design of [[Cryptographic protocol|cryptographic protocols]] that perform operations—such as [[encryption]], decryption, [[key exchange]], and [[authentication]]—on multiple inputs simultaneously, rather than processing each input individually.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Zhenfu Cao |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=T2wkaz8lUEAC |title=New Directions of Modern Cryptography |date=2012 |publisher=CRC Press, Taylor & Francis Group |isbn=9781466501386 |location=Boca Raton |page=171}}</ref> Batching cryptographic operations can significantly reduce the marginal cost of handling individual inputs—a principle that was first introduced by Amos Fiat in 1989.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Amos Fiat |date=1997 |title=Batch RSA |journal=Journal of Cryptology |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=75–88 |doi=10.1007/s001459900021 |s2cid=15613430}}</ref>
